forces.title: Payments sector IT spending to compound 9% annually through 2030
forces.description: Global payments industry IT expenditures are projected to increase at a compound annual growth rate of approximately 9 percent through 2030. This growth significantly outpaces the moderated 4 percent annual growth forecast for global payments revenue. This substantial investment is driven by the need for operational efficiency, technological leadership, and adaptation to structural shifts like agentic AI. For IT Services & Outsourcing providers, this represents a strong, sustained demand for custom application development, system integration, cloud migration, and managed services within the financial sector in Europe.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Value shifting to invisible control layer in payments due to agentic AI
forces.description: The payments industry is undergoing a structural transition where value is relocating from visible front-end checkouts to an 'invisible control layer.' This layer encompasses back-end trust, machine identity, consent engines, and dynamic routing protocols governed by autonomous software agents. This shift necessitates significant investment in new IT infrastructure and services for financial institutions and payment operators. IT Services & Outsourcing firms will experience high demand for custom application development, system integration, and IT consulting to build, implement, and manage these complex, secure, and dynamically routed payment systems.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Agentic AI threatens $75-160 billion in global payments revenue by 2030
forces.description: Agentic Artificial Intelligence is projected to put roughly $75 billion in global payments revenue at risk by 2030 in a base case scenario, potentially reaching $160 billion in an aggressive scenario. This disruption impacts retail and commercial deposits through yield compression and balance migration, and consumer credit card revenues via payment rail substitution and fee avoidance. This significant threat compels financial institutions to invest heavily in IT Services & Outsourcing to develop new, defensible revenue streams, optimize existing operations, and implement AI-driven cost reduction strategies to mitigate the revenue pressure.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Agentic payments create new high-margin monetizable infrastructure service opportunities
forces.description: The transition to agentic payments introduces transactions that cannot be safely executed with current service sets, creating new monetizable infrastructure service opportunities. These include developing agent credentials, mandate and consent management, robust risk controls, agent wallets, and transaction protection frameworks. These new service pools are expected to monetize differently from base payment flows, generating recurring per-mandate fees, per-call API pricing, and risk-bearing premiums, leading to potentially lucrative margin structures (up to 80%). This offers a significant upside for IT Services & Outsourcing firms specializing in custom application development and system integration for these advanced payment capabilities.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Agentic AI unlocks $110 billion in productivity value for payment providers
forces.description: Agentic AI is poised to unlock up to $110 billion in annual productivity value across the payments industry, particularly in Europe. This value is concentrated in customer operations ($50 billion) and software engineering & IT ($30 billion), driven by 20-25% structural efficiency gains in software development and 15-20% productivity improvements in customer contacts. This significant productivity prize translates into strong demand for IT Services & Outsourcing, as payments providers seek expert assistance in implementing AI-driven automation, optimizing software engineering processes, and enhancing operational efficiency through custom application development, system integration, and IT consulting.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Enterprise AI focus shifting to application layer, redesigning business processes
forces.description: Enterprises are moving beyond AI experimentation to actively redesign legacy business processes, shifting the competitive focus to the application layer of the AI tech stack. This requires software capable of understanding specific workflows, operating within existing enterprise systems, and automating tasks in complex environments. This fundamental structural change in AI adoption drives substantial demand for IT Services & Outsourcing, including extensive IT consulting for process redesign, custom application development for specialized AI solutions, and system integration to embed AI within core enterprise workflows in Europe.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: European AI application funding surges, reaching 44% of US levels
forces.description: Venture capital funding for European AI application start-ups saw a significant surge, climbing to €6.8 billion in the first half of 2026, representing 44 percent of comparable US funding levels—a substantial increase from just 11 percent in 2018. This robust influx of capital directly fuels the growth of companies specializing in custom software development and AI application integration within Europe. Consequently, IT Services & Outsourcing providers will experience increased demand to support these rapidly scaling AI-native firms and their enterprise clients in developing and implementing advanced AI solutions.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: European corporates boost investment and partnerships in AI application ventures
forces.description: European corporates are becoming more active strategic co-investors and partners in AI application ventures, with their participation in VC deal value growing from 14 percent of US levels in 2018 to 39 percent in H1 2026. Initiatives like the EU AI Champions are unlocking significant co-investments and partnerships. This trend provides AI application start-ups (and by extension, IT Services & Outsourcing firms) with crucial access to complex workflows, proprietary data, and powerful distribution channels, accelerating enterprise-grade deployments and driving demand for specialized IT consulting, system integration, and custom development services in Europe.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: European AI deployments accelerate to 4-6 months, enhancing market agility
forces.description: Successful European AI deployments are significantly accelerating, moving from strategy to shipped feature in just four to six months, a notable improvement from the previous 12 to 18 months. This increased speed of implementation reflects enhanced market agility and a more efficient ecosystem for AI adoption. For IT Services & Outsourcing providers, this trend indicates a rising demand for agile development methodologies, efficient project management, and rapid deployment capabilities, enabling them to capitalize on faster client investment cycles and contribute to quicker time-to-value for AI solutions across European industries.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: Agentic AI transforms maintenance, boosting efficiency in asset-heavy sectors
forces.description: Agentic AI is revolutionizing maintenance and reliability operations across asset-heavy industries such as mining, energy, rail, and airlines. Examples include a US oil and gas company reducing update time by 80% with gen-AI workflows and a packaging manufacturer increasing technician productivity by 85% with an AI scheduling tool. This transformation drives significant demand for IT Services & Outsourcing firms to develop and implement AI-driven solutions for predictive maintenance, asset health monitoring, optimized planning, and automated execution, leading to enhanced operational efficiency and substantial cost savings for clients in these sectors.
forces.source_title: Maintenance meets AI: A proven approach for asset-heavy industries

forces.title: Adversarial AI in payments drives demand for advanced real-time trust systems
forces.description: The emergence of adversarial AI and a trust deficit in agentic payment environments necessitates a shift towards robust, real-time fraud mitigation and trust-scoring systems. Traditional human-centric fraud screening is ineffective at machine-to-machine speeds, requiring continuous machine authentication, behavioral trust scoring, and sub-millisecond policy verification embedded within transaction flows. This critical need creates significant demand for IT Services & Outsourcing firms specializing in cybersecurity, identity management, and advanced AI/ML-driven risk management solutions, as financial institutions and payment networks seek to build a secure control layer for autonomous transactions.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Agentic treasury risks ERP-to-bank inversion, commoditizing banks
forces.description: The rise of independent platforms and venture-backed entrants building autonomous treasury agents poses a significant disintermediation risk for commercial banks, potentially reducing them to commodity utilities. These agents manage cash positioning, working capital, and payment execution dynamically, sourcing liquidity and rails from optimal providers. If third-party software agents hold the client mandate, banks risk losing direct corporate relationships. This 'ERP-to-bank inversion' creates an urgent imperative for banks to invest heavily in proprietary agentic advisory capabilities and IT Services & Outsourcing to develop custom solutions and consulting expertise to maintain their competitive edge.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Europe experiences net inflow of AI professionals, boosting talent pool
forces.description: Europe is witnessing a significant reversal in transatlantic AI talent flows, with a net inflow of AI professionals from the United States for the first time in years during 2025. Countries like Germany rank high globally for skilled AI talent, and the UK remains a strong magnet. This growing talent pool, coupled with narrowing pay gaps and proactive university initiatives in venture building, provides a robust foundation for IT Services & Outsourcing firms in Europe. It enhances their capacity to develop and deliver advanced AI-driven solutions and services, strengthening the region's overall competitiveness in the AI application space.
forces.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

forces.title: Irish Food & Beverage prioritizes automation, digitalization, AI for productivity
forces.description: The Irish Food and Beverage sector is actively prioritizing investment in automation, digitalization, and AI technologies to enhance productivity and competitiveness. This strategic focus, observed by Bank of Ireland, is driven by the need to manage high staffing and operating costs, strengthen supply chain resilience, and meet evolving consumer and regulatory expectations regarding sustainability. This trend generates direct and sustained demand for IT Services & Outsourcing firms in Ireland, offering custom application development, system integration, cloud migration, and managed services to support the digital transformation initiatives within this critical sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

viewpoints.title: Europe well-positioned for AI application layer growth amid business process redesign
viewpoints.description: McKinsey views Europe as well-positioned to thrive in the next phase of AI value creation, specifically in transforming complex, everyday business processes. European companies are adept at deep integration into highly regulated and heterogeneous environments, which is increasingly crucial as AI shifts from general-purpose intelligence to specialized deployment. This competitive focus on the application layer, requiring software that understands specific workflows and automates work within existing enterprise systems, plays to Europe's strengths, including deep industrial expertise and regulatory rigor. This outlook indicates strong growth potential for IT Services & Outsourcing firms in Europe that specialize in AI application development and system integration.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

viewpoints.title: AI applications to remain distinct, capturing majority of future tech ecosystem value
viewpoints.description: McKinsey suggests that AI applications will remain a distinct and valuable segment, not subsumed by foundational models. This is supported by the need for different talent profiles, such as deployment engineers and knowledge experts, to embed AI deeply within customer workflows. Historically, major technological shifts have seen value creation shift significantly to the application layer, which captured 70-85% of the ecosystem value in past cycles like the internet/cloud and mobile. This indicates a robust and long-lasting opportunity for IT Services & Outsourcing providers specializing in application development, integration, and consulting for AI.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

viewpoints.title: Europe poised to build global leaders in complex vertical software solutions
viewpoints.description: A global enterprise software executive, as cited by McKinsey, affirms Europe's strong capability to develop and scale leading companies in vertical software, particularly for complex environments and deep, specific solutions. This perspective highlights Europe's inherent strengths in specialized domains, which enable its IT Services & Outsourcing firms to deliver tailored, compliance-ready AI applications for enterprise clients globally. This strategic focus on vertical expertise positions European IT services companies for significant competitive advantage and growth in the evolving AI landscape.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity

viewpoints.title: Irish Food & Drink sector embraces AI for practical, operational improvements
viewpoints.description: The Bank of Ireland observes that AI adoption in Ireland's Food and Drink sector is transitioning from experimental phases to practical implementation. This shift is driving investment in AI solutions for critical operational areas, including quality control, predictive maintenance, production planning, and supply chain management. Public and private sector initiatives, such as those from Enterprise Ireland and Bank of Ireland, are actively supporting businesses in exploring and deploying these AI solutions. This trend represents a positive demand driver for IT Services & Outsourcing firms in Ireland, providing expertise in custom application development, system integration, and managed services for AI.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

viewpoints.title: AI rewiring demands joint business-IT accountability, moving beyond IT projects
viewpoints.description: McKinsey emphasizes that rewiring operations with AI is not merely an IT project where the business provides requirements for IT to deliver. Instead, it necessitates a collaborative, agile operating model where business, technology, and other team members work together and are jointly accountable for performance improvement. This indicates a structural shift in how IT services are consumed and delivered for AI initiatives. While presenting a challenge to traditional IT engagement models, it also represents a significant opportunity for IT Services & Outsourcing firms capable of offering integrated consulting, co-creation, and agile development approaches to their clients.
viewpoints.source_title: Maintenance meets AI: A proven approach for asset-heavy industries
